data.exact_reserve_text: In 2016, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m (2015: GBP 27.1m) due primarily to a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts following lower than expected incurred claims movements during 2016 and a release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account as policies come off risk.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Reduction in assessment of medical malpractice claims on 2013 and prior accounts leading to favourable development and contributing to a GBP 20.1m overall surplus in ultimate claims.

prior_year_events.event_name: Release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account
prior_year_events.impact_description: Release of catastrophe loadings as 2015 policies come off risk, contributing to favourable prior year development.

named_events.loss_description: Expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account stated as GBP 88.5m, of which GBP 69.6m had been incurred at year end (mentioned in syndicate commentary).

named_events.event_name: International catastrophe events (Chile, New Zealand, Japan, Thailand)
named_events.loss_description: Grouped international catastrophe events of 2010/11 referenced; gross incurred losses from these events across all years were disclosed (GBP 25.5m) with a further provision (GBP 3.6m).

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2016 Syndicate 2791 had gross claims outstanding of GBP 321.0m. During 2016 the syndicate recorded an overall gross favourable development (release) in prior years' ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m ( -6.3% of opening gross reserves). The release was driven principally by a reduction in estimated medical malpractice claims on 2013 and earlier years and by releases of catastrophe loadings as 2015 policies came off risk. The movements primarily affected long-tail casualty/professional lines and catastrophe-exposed property/reinsurance business.
raw_causal_phrases: an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m
a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts
a release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account as policies come off risk
The movement in the net provision for claims includes a release of GBP 26.7m in respect of claims outstanding at the previous year end

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) was taken from the explicit narrative note stating an 'overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m' (gross). A gross claims development triangle is provided but includes an aggregate '2010 and prior' column which cannot be used for diagonal comparisons; the triangle was used only for cross-checks. There is some potential distortion due to Reinsurance-to-Close (RITC) activity between Syndicate 2791 and Syndicate 6103 referenced elsewhere; RITC transactions can distort development patterns. Some LOB-specific movements are described qualitatively (e.g. medical malpractice, catastrophe loads) but not quantified in isolation; amounts for those LOBs are therefore null.
